correctness.rationale: The exact JR obstruction is |N_z\U(W)|>=ceil(n/k). For k=2, if n is odd any quota-sized candidate covers a strict majority; if even any pair of quota-sized candidates with different supporter sets covers more than half. The identical-support exception requires exclusion of every available candidate containing the full uncovered complement. For every non-DR JR two-seat committee in a DR-feasible election, the proof exhausts high-, exact-, and below-quota support cases and constructs an allowed strict JR-preserving swap. The two-low case uses JR of the original pair to prove the complementary swap works whenever the first fails. In the explicit six-voter example both committees and both potential strict improving swaps are checked directly. verify.py independently corroborates 211380 distinct-support profiles, 18000 seeded duplicate-allowing profiles and the trap. No finite check is substituted for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The September 2026 primary source defines DR and Local DR and proves termination of local search and general hardness; its explicit locally trapped instance has four seats. The new results establish exact two-seat global correctness of every local optimum, a parity-sensitive support criterion including duplicate labels, and a three-seat local trap using five genuinely distinct candidate supporter sets. These are distinct implications from generic JR existence or mere local-search termination. Source and published-finding corpus searches found no equivalent, with residual risks stated.

The older JR source and price-of-JR work were reviewed through accessible summaries, not exhaustively through full text; they are background rather than the source of the new DR objective.
Self-review is not independent peer review.

value.rationale: The motivating work explicitly exhibits a local optimum missing a feasible exact DR committee, so the size at which that failure first becomes possible is a natural question about a proposed fair-representation rule. The new two-seat theorem shows every local optimum is exact whenever exactness is feasible, not merely that brute-force search is polynomial for fixed k. A six-voter five-candidate instance with distinct supporter sets shows that the guarantee fails immediately at three seats. The parity-sensitive feasibility criterion handles candidate-label multiplicity and admits linear scanning. No general theorem for larger committee sizes is claimed.
